gemini.rationale: The transaction was a whole-company cash acquisition where ARRIS became a wholly-owned subsidiary of CommScope. The entire legal entity, products, operations, and workforce transferred together, with no documented structural mismatch between products and processes (gap_45 = 0) or processes and organization (gap_56 = 0) at closing.

grok.rationale: The deal was a whole-company cash scheme of arrangement under which ARRIS became an indirect wholly-owned CommScope subsidiary at the April 4, 2019 Effective Time, so the CPE/Network & Cloud/Enterprise Networks customer-facing product tier crossed together with the operating entity that housed its processes; no product-vs-process mismatch is documented at closing (gap_45=0). Rank-and-file workforce continuity with a one-year compensation/benefits floor was contracted while only the officer/director layer was replaced by CommScope personnel—standard change-of-control governance, not a structural process-without-organization gap (gap_56=0). No TSA or shared-substrate bridge was located, consistent with entire-entity transfer rather than a carve-out.

openai.rationale: The acquisition covered all issued and to-be-issued ARRIS shares, and at the Effective Time ARRIS became an indirect wholly owned CommScope subsidiary; the closing summary states that ARRIS's product/customer-facing business was carried into the combined company, with no documented separation from its operating processes. The rank-and-file workforce was carried into the combined company with a one-year compensation and benefits continuity floor, while all ARRIS officers and directors were replaced by CommScope personnel, so no closing-structure process-versus-organization gap is documented.
